citation: Sun Kwok. (2017). Science Education in the 21st Century. Submitted to Nature Astronomy. https://www.nature.com/natastronomy
title: HKU Science Foundation courses: two required integrated courses teaching method and concepts over computation
description: A sequence of two one-semester courses required of all incoming science students regardless of intended major, introduced at HKU in 2012. The first teaches the scientific method, logical and quantitative reasoning, and mathematics through "the formulation of problems but not calculations"; the second surveys physics, astronomy, earth sciences, chemistry and biology to give "an overview of natural science" with unifying concepts. The courses start with real-life problems, and exams present new situations rather than lecture tasks.
requirements: Required of all incoming science students irrespective of intended major
Shared teaching and assessment techniques including history of subject and exam items with new situations
target_learning_goals: broad integrated view of the sciences
examples: Course content listed includes scientific method, guesstimation, mathematical modelling, hypothesis testing, correlation and causation, regression, and predictions
key_sources: Sun Kwok. (2017). Science Education in the 21st Century. Submitted to Nature Astronomy. https://www.nature.com/natastronomy

article_title: A Comparative Analysis of Student Performance Predictions in Online Courses using Heterogeneous Knowledge Graphs
citation: Trask, T., Lytle, N., Boyle, M., Joyner, D., & Mubarak, A. (2024). A Comparative Analysis of Student Performance Predictions in Online Courses using Heterogeneous Knowledge Graphs. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.12153
title: Heterogeneous Knowledge Graph representation of online learning environments for GCN-based student performance prediction
description: A framework representing online learning environments as heterogeneous knowledge graphs with students, course videos, assessments, and pages as node types, and student-content interactions as weighted edges. Student-video edges encode normalized percentage of video watched; student-assessment edges encode first grade, final grade, and number of attempts; student-page edges encode binary success criteria (>70% on assessments or videos). A Graph Convolutional Network with Sage Convolution layers processes this graph to derive edge-level predictions of whether a student passed a particular page. The article applies this to identify at-risk students and compare engagement patterns across course modalities.
requirements: Clickstream data from an online learning platform with video interactions and assessment submissions
Course content linked via shared page properties
Assessment scores as ground truth labels
constraints: Only 30% of course videos and assessments could be directly linked to course pages via the page property
Mobile app events were excluded due to inability to link page content
target_learners: On-campus undergraduates in introductory computer science
target_learning_goals: Predicting student pass/fail outcomes on problem sets
Identifying at-risk students for early intervention
examples: Applied to Georgia Tech's GTX1301 Introduction to Python course with 5 on-campus and 2 online instances on EdX, using 16M on-campus and 55M online clickstream events
